# sam_recon

Historical reconstruction of Apogee's **Secret Agent** (1992), episodes 1-3 (`SAM1.EXE`,
`SAM2.EXE`, `SAM3.EXE`): readable Turbo Pascal 5.0 and TASM source in [game/](game/) that the
original toolchain compiles back into the original programs.

Original game files and anything derived from them (unpacked images, builds) are never committed;
supply them in `assets/` (or `$SAM_ASSET_DIR`).

## Result

`game/` is built with the pinned Turbo Pascal 5.0 (TPC, TURBO.TPL), Turbo Assembler 1.0 and compared
with the originals (`python tools/verify.py`):

| Episode | Load image | Equal bytes | Residue bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SAM1 | 188,736 | 188,644 | 92 |
| SAM2 | 189,744 | 189,664 | 80 |
| SAM3 | 189,792 | 189,761 | 31 |

Every byte of code (the game, the Genus PCX Toolkit 3.56 and ProGraphx 2.0 libraries, and Borland's
System/Crt/Dos runtime), every initialised data byte, the relocation set and the header fields of the
load image are identical. The only differences are inside the 102 bytes per episode of undefined
(`DB ?`) storage in two linked assembly objects, which the original build filled with leftover
compiler memory (fragments of the original source text and symbol tables in SAM1/SAM2; traced in
[docs/object-holes.md](docs/object-holes.md)). They are documented residue (`config/residue.json`),
compared and reported, never filled or patched; consequently the LZEXE-packed files are not equal.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| [game/](game/) | the source: SAM.PAS (program), SAMPLAY, SAMLEVEL, SAMUI, SAMSOUND, SAMDATA, TEXT80, GAMEJOY, PCXGENUS, PROGRPHX units, six .ASM objects, BUILD.BAT; episode differences as `{$IFDEF SAMn}` |
| tools/ | `oracle.py` (lock, decode, cross-check), `lz91.py`, `lz91_emulate.py`, `repack.py`, `verify.py` (build + compare), `validate.py`, `assets.py` (asset decoder) |
| config/ | oracle lock, pinned toolchain hashes, compiler profile, residue ranges |
| [port/](port/) | the SDL3 port: emulated PC + SDL3 front end, TP 5.0 runtime, the assembly objects in C; the game code is generated from game/ by `tools/pas2c.py` ([port/README.md](port/README.md)) |
| docs/ | [oracle](docs/oracle.md), [compiler](docs/compiler.md), [assembly libraries](docs/assembly.md), [object holes](docs/object-holes.md), [file formats](docs/formats.md), [actors](docs/actors.md), [runtime model](docs/runtime.md), [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md), [names and evidence](docs/names.json) |

## Requirements

* Python 3.11 with `capstone` 5.0.9 and `unicorn` 2.1.4 (`python tools/setup_env.py` vendors them
  into `build/python`).
* Pinned tools outside the repository (hashes in `config/toolchain.json`): Turbo Pascal 5.0,
  TASM 1.0, MS-DOS Player (`C:\tools\nmlgcdos`), DOSBox-X and LZEXE 0.91 for packing.

```bash
python tools/setup_env.py
python tools/validate.py            # oracle, build of game/ for all three episodes, tests
python tools/validate.py --crosscheck --pack
python tools/validate.py --dos    # run game/BUILD.BAT itself in DOSBox-X
python tools/validate.py --port   # also build the SDL3 port and boot SAM1-3 to their title screens
```

`game/` is independent of this repository: under DOS, `BUILD 1`, `BUILD 2` or `BUILD 3` with TPC,
TASM and LZEXE on the PATH produces `SAM.EXE` (the unpacked program compared above) and the
packed `SAMn.EXE` ([game/README.md](game/README.md)).

## History

The reconstruction followed the method of the sibling project duke1_recon: locked oracle -> census
and cross-episode atlas -> every routine proven byte-identical in a harness that reproduced the
original data segment (GPT-6 Luna / GPT-6.1 Sol workers, supervised) -> declaration consolidation ->
whole-program link -> standalone tree -> readability passes. The per-routine sources, recipes and the
matching tools are preserved in the git tag `matching-archive`. Current phase: an SDL3/Android port
generated from `game/` ([docs/port.md](docs/port.md), [port/README.md](port/README.md)).

kandowontu2-hocus-native-docs-parity-aud.text:
# Registered-v1.1 function parity audit

## Result

The native port has an implementation for every observable game-owned path
reachable with the registered-v1.1 executable, archive, and save format. The
deterministic tests lock the recovered gameplay rules, front-end policies,
logical 320x200 raster, timers, saves, demos, sound dispatch, and all official
level data. DOS runtime, VGA, interrupt, and audio-driver routines terminate at
explicit native service boundaries; they are not instruction translations.

One deliberately excluded path remains: enemy selector 7 is absent from all
360 registered `.007` records and appears to perform an invalid-index memory
write. The native implementation does not reproduce undefined memory
corruption for a fabricated level. This does not affect any registered level,
demo, save, menu, or normal input path.

This report uses three distinct terms:

1. **Inventory parity** means all code-entry targets reached by direct control
   flow and every range-validated table have been counted, and every observed
   indirect transfer has an assigned type.
2. **Behavioral parity** means a recovered DOS rule has a native equivalent and
   a focused deterministic regression test.
3. **Instruction parity** is neither possible nor required for a native Win32
   rewrite of DOS, VGA, timer, input, and audio services.

`registered_v1_1_disassembly_inventory` regenerates the analysis and locks the
current conservative inventory at **649 code-entry targets**, **35,327
instructions**, and **91,942 instruction bytes**. Of the 649 targets, 158 are
labels recovered from 21 bounded near-jump tables. The game-owned segments
contain 154 targets and the runtime/platform/audio segments contain 495.
The seeds comprise **234 relocation-validated immediate far transfers**, **158
bounded jump-table targets**, and **one explicitly verified installed callback**;
the test suite locks those counts as well as the final traversal totals.
`registered_v1_1_parity_ledger` independently parses this report and the
generated JSON inventory. It fails on a missing, duplicate, or spurious
game-owned address, so the human ledger cannot drift silently from the binary.

All **67 indirect transfers are classified**:

| Class | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Range-validated near-jump tables | 21 | Selector transform, upper bound, table extent, and targets verified from the image |
| Typed dynamic callbacks | 45 | Borland runtime callbacks or selected audio-driver method slots |
| Decoder artifact | 1 | Operand bytes following Borland software-8087 `INT 34h..3Dh` encoding, not an executed far jump |
| Unresolved | **0** | No unassigned indirect site remains |

## Corrections made by the current audit

The instruction-led replay found and corrected these native mismatches:

- The level tick now preserves the DOS collision, pending-spawn, enemy-shot,
  enemy-update, and distant-release phase order.
- Camera state is persistent and advances by the recovered horizontal
  half-tile and vertical tile increments instead of snapping directly to
  Hocus.
- Ordinary enemies now keep the separate DOS launch countdown, attack-pose
  timer, animation delay/reset words, vertical sentinel, and hit-flash parity.
- The shared enemy tail increments and loops movement/attack frames in the DOS
  order, including the every-other-update gate and common firing RNG draw.
- Enemy projectile height is no longer inflated twice. Moving and stationary
  shots use the recovered spawn anchors, directional filter, delay, render
  snapshot, and boss zero-delay behavior.
- Enemy hit flash uses the fixed palette-`0x70` opaque mask from
  `0BA5:2896`, and high-health/boss enemies draw the recovered 78-column health
  bar.
- Hocus's lightning now probes the direction-specific current-position tile
  patterns before moving. Breakable tiles create a Twink; ordinary walls create
  the 16-particle burst at the recovered east, west, and vertical offsets.
- The complete stored-laser path is audited in `LASER_AUDIT.md`. Pickup,
  inventory/blink state, shot creation and ammo use, frames, wall/effect paths,
  instant-kill/piercing collision, sounds, and BANANA semantics match. The
  indicator's previously missing initial 14-pixel upward offset was corrected.
- The disassembler now follows all 21 validated jump tables. This exposed 156
  additional code-entry targets and 20 additional indirect sites; all are
  typed and regression-locked.
- `0B97:0001` now runs the recovered piracy, Apogee, and registered-title
  sequence with its 40/20/30-step VGA fades, 15/9/4-second holds, one-shot
  fanfare, looping title music, and startup VOC. Its `1392:0108` waits accept
  input by advancing only the current screen rather than bypassing the rest.
- `06B8:19A4` and `2259` now drive the generic DOS menu presentation: the
  original `HOCUS.IMG`/`BOTTOM.IMG` composition, proportional font metrics,
  row palette ramps, heading and `~` spacing rules, animated eight-frame cursor
  copied from the startup-hidden `BULLIT.IMG` raster on VGA page 3, 75-star
  `SINCOS.DAT`/`RANDOM.DAT` field, first-letter navigation,
  persistent group selections, and 20-retrace entry/exit fades.
- Window painting now publishes a fully composed back buffer in one `BitBlt`;
  the prior direct black clear could become visible between timer frames.
- The original Borland `srand`/`rand` LCG now selects attract demos randomly
  modulo five instead of cycling sequentially.
- Configurable viewport look-up/look-down controls, joystick buttons three and
  four, joystick-exclusive gameplay bindings, and the original two-sample
  direction confirmation are recovered.
- Native XInput support checks all four controller slots through a dynamically
  loaded Windows API, provides fixed modern-pad mappings and dead zones, skips
  legacy calibration, and falls back to the recovered WinMM joystick path.
- The crystal HUD preserves the executable's first-decimal-character rule;
  values above nine are not silently clamped to nine.
- A newly started Episode 1 campaign displays `CRYSTAL.IMG` at the recovered
  Mode-X position (48,46) and blocks for keyboard or joystick input. Restarts,
  restores, and attract demos pass the original zero flag and do not show it.
- Crystal pickup flashes now resolve indices `0x6F..0x76` through the active
  `GAMEPAL.PAL` half instead of the backdrop PCX's unused black placeholders.
- `HOCUS.DAT` is a Windows resource and runtime archive reads are memory-backed.
  The native executable nevertheless requires the exact registered-v1.1
  `HOCUS.EXE` in its own folder as an ownership/version check; it validates the
  file but never executes it or reads game assets from it.
- The full registered event family is now present: `.005` insertion records
  56..80, `.006` removal records 81..105, teleporters, switches, keyholes,
  enemy triggers, and the alternating `0BA5:2C81` pending-gate/tile updater.
- Event replay corrected final-treasure sound nine, post-dispatch health
  clamping, firepower upgrades saved during super shot, repeated completed
  switches, and side-cell gate activation.
- The gameplay raster now snapshots map, HUD, player, enemy-projectile, enemy,
  pickup, Twinkle, explosion, and spell-trail state at each DOS draw point.
  Crystal flash replaces only the map page; actors/effects remain above it.
- Enemy spawn countdowns draw randomized Twinkles only. The player teleporter's
  five-frame Morph record is no longer drawn over spawning enemies.
- Enemy creation selectors four and five now apply their exact frame/direction
  initialization, and health bars plus visual effects retain the DOS per-slot
  and inter-routine overlap order.
- Native save discovery is confined to `HOCUS.SAV` beside the executable. A
  development build cannot find or overwrite the original save in a parent
  source directory.

The asset/gameplay smoke test now locks east, west, and vertical lightning-wall
effects, breakable-wall Twinks, boss pre-action rendering, boss zero-delay
shots, the boss health raster, enemy attack/animation counters, phase order,
camera movement, sprite metadata, events, pickups, hazards, saves, results,
audio conversion, and demo playback.

## Complete discovered-code boundary

The 495 non-game targets are accounted for at the native boundary. They are
native replacements, not translations of DOS services:

| Segment(s) | Targets | DOS responsibility | Native boundary |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `0000` | 199 | Borland startup, C runtime, formatted I/O, DOS files/memory/strings, floating-point helpers | C++ runtime, filesystem, Win32 process startup |
| `05D8` | 28 | VGA modes, planes, palette, image loading/copying | indexed decoders, framebuffer composition, GDI presentation |
| `068C` | 9 | archive allocation/read/write helpers | `DatArchive` and typed decoders |
| `124A` | 4 | planar image/sprite transforms | decoded sprite frames and native blits |
| `136B` | 6 | logical sound/music facade | deterministic sound events and WinMM services |
| `1392` | 18 | timers, input, random table, waits, file wrappers | fixed tick, Win32 input/timing, `RANDOM.DAT` state |
| `1437`..`1CF4` | 231 | hardware audio, MIDI, joystick, interrupt and driver support | WinMM/MCI/joystick services or platform-inapplicable code |

Replacing these services is correct for a native port. It also means “every
DOS function has an identical native function” is not a valid certification
criterion; observable behavior at each boundary is the relevant criterion.

## Game-owned code ledger

Every one of the 154 discovered game-owned targets is included below. Labels
inside a bounded jump table are listed with their owning dispatcher.

### Startup and top-level control (18)

| Addresses | Recovered role | Audit status |
|---|---|---|
| `0548:0014` | global data/archive/audio/random initialization | Native replacement; DOS allocation and hardware setup are platform-inapplicable |
| `0548:035A`, `0570`, `05C2`, `0736`, `0745`, `0776`, `07A8`, `07FA`, `0802`, `081F`, `083E`, `0891`, `089A`, `08A4`, `08AB`, `08B2` | top-level state machine plus main/in-game dispatch tables | Recovered state flow, attract selection, level transitions, shortcuts, settings, and exit policies implemented |
| `0B97:0001` | piracy/Apogee/title startup presentation and audio sequence | Behaviorally recovered and timing-tested |

### Front end, saves, pages, and results (79)

| Addresses | Recovered role | Audit status |
|---|---|---|
| `06B8:000C`, `0080`, `0103`, `039C`, `05E9`, `071F`, `087C`, `0901`, `094B` | input polling, menu background, font width/draw primitives | Generic-menu observable behavior recovered; Win32 supplies equivalent key events and 14 ms retrace pacing |
| `06B8:0B21`, `0D99`, `0E52`, `0F3D`, `0FBC`, `10AC`, `1316`, `137D`, `1744`, `17DA`, `19A4`, `1BAE` | option strings, prompts, key definition, volume/control screens, menu composition, name input | Exact recovered strings, logical rasters, navigation, capacities, and DOS setting fields implemented |
| `06B8:1C9B`, `2018`, `2203`, `2216`, `221E`, `2226`, `222E`, `2236`, `223E`, `2246`, `2259` | high scores, bounded front-end action dispatch, generic navigation | Recovered signed score ordering, name editing, action tables, selection persistence, and attract baseline implemented |
| `06B8:24C3`, `24DC`, `24F5`, `2527`, `2540`, `2559`, `2578` | menu/screen wrappers and notice handling | Recovered wrapper flow, fades, prompts, and return policies implemented |
| `06B8:25CC`, `2B8B`, `2EE1` | save, restore, quit confirmation | Nine-slot raster, separate cursors, editing, exact 990-byte fields, and Y/N/Escape confirmation implemented |
| `06B8:2F16` | joystick-centering calibration | Center capture, one-third thresholds, fire-button choice, cancellation, and direction reset implemented through WinMM |
| `06B8:2FA8`, `3048`, `30DE`, `3187` | front-end presentation wrappers | Observable copy/fade/return behavior implemented at the native framebuffer boundary |
| `06B8:3230`, `3401`, `364D`, `3899`, `3AE5`, `3D31`, `3F7D` | story/help/order/credits/ending page viewers and footer | Both page layouts, picture records, spacing, PgUp/PgDn/Home/End controls, joystick mapping, prompts, and fades implemented |
| `06B8:407D`, `40BD`, `40FD`, `413D`, `417D`, `41BD`, `429A`, `42CB`, `44CC` | page/title/credit/ending wrappers | All registered wrapper sequences and timed credit behavior implemented |
| `06B8:4600`, `4679`, `4683`, `4689`, `469B`, `46A2`, `46A5`, `46D5`, `4707`, `476B`, `4772`, `4795`, `47B3`, `4806` | final presentation and its two bounded menu dispatch tables | Pause/finale dispatch, ending transitions, resume/restart/save/restore/options/quit policies implemented |
| `06B8:4889`, `4D76` | level results/bonuses and terminal presentation | Exact text selection/layout, signed formulas, time tables, score banking, WARP raster/audio, and transition sequence implemented |

### Level engine (57)

| Addresses | Recovered role | Audit status |
|---|---|---|
| `0BA5:0006`, `00D3`, `01B6`, `0267`, `0439`, `04D3` | enemy-shot/body/player collision, kill-all, Hocus-shot collision, release, creation | Behaviorally recovered and phase-ordered with focused tests |
| `0BA5:0720`, `0741`, `0795`, `07E8`, `0841`, `0864`, `0887`, `08B4`, `08E6` | enemy creation selectors 0..8 | Registered selectors are covered; selector 7 is dormant in all `.007` data and the native safe arc does not reproduce its apparent original out-of-bounds write |
| `0BA5:0922`, `0A81`, `0C5B`, `0CE8`, `1019`, `126C`, `147D`, `1555`, `160F`, `16CF`, `182B`, `195B`, `1AB1`, `1AD7` | enemy projectiles, health bar, E3/E4 bosses, enemy loop, active behaviors, shared attack/animation tail | Recovered registered paths are implemented and regression-tested, including RNG, delay, snapshot, attack, hit-flash, and boss timing |
| `0BA5:1FAA`, `20B1`, `2174`, `21C6` | Twinks and spell-trail pools | Pool sizes, counters, and state are implemented; VGA-plane draw timing is a native raster replacement |
| `0BA5:220F`, `2242`, `23BA`, `249E`, `25FF`, `26B3`, `27E2`, `2896` | palette fade, sprite loading, morph and directional/masked sprite variants | Six-bit palette effects, sprite variants, masks, crystal flash, and hit-flash behavior implemented in the logical framebuffer |
| `0BA5:29C5`, `2C81` | incremental camera; alternating visible tile animation and pending gate mutation | Recovered persistent camera order/increments, countdowns, tile modes, and off-screen gate progression are implemented and tested |
| `0BA5:2E9D`, `2F1C`, `2FF3` | pending enemy spawns and eight-slot/16-particle explosions | Behaviorally implemented with corrected phase and draw snapshots |
| `0BA5:3125`, `3297`, `348D` | HUD numeric primitives and HUD update | Original digit/key cells, positions, centering, flash cycle, and first-character crystal quirk implemented |
| `0BA5:3643`, `3684`, `36F0` | crystal counting and pickup sparkle allocation/update | Behaviorally implemented and tested |
| `0BA5:3751`, `37FC`, `38B6` | pause/message presentation | Exact shadow/foreground raster and any-key/two-button modal policy implemented without advancing the level |
| `0BA5:39F3` | complete registered event dispatcher | All registered event families have native paths and focused tests |
| `0BA5:453A` | level loader and monolithic fixed-step runner | Registered gameplay phase/draw order is recovered; platform timing, pause/presentation integration, and the dormant selector divergence remain |

## Native boundary qualifications

- The dormant selector-7 invalid-memory side effect is intentionally excluded,
  as described above.
- Win32, GDI, DirectSound, MCI, and WinMM replace DOS interrupts, VGA ports,

"""Projectile physics integrator - function-for-function port of the v1.5 engine.

Ground truth (READ-ONLY RE, binary never executed):
  FUN_2a4a_02f2  shot driver / fixed-step loop (decompiles/FUN_2a4a_02f2.c)
  FUN_2a4a_0763  spawn: seeds pos/vel, +0x4c guidance cb (FUN_2a4a_0763.c)
  FUN_2a4a_01c4  per-shot dt/grav/wind scalar setup (FUN_2a4a_01c4.c)
  FUN_2a4a_0b1f  per-step integrator + bounce apply (FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c)
  FUN_2a4a_1349  projectile-vs-boundary handler (FUN_2a4a_1349.c)
  FUN_2a4a_1f5a  reposition/redraw at boundary (FUN_2a4a_1f5a.c)
  FUN_2a4a_2228  DETONATION dispatch (FUN_2a4a_2228.c) -> "die" in this port

Wall sub-modes (catalogs/04_menus_ui.md:414, 03_config_schema.md:113):
  NONE      no effect (fly off; tracked to EDGES_EXTEND then removed)
  CONCRETE  bounce, white  - side/ceiling reflect coef -2.0
  PADDED    absorb, green  - side/ceiling reflect coef -0.5
  RUBBER    bounce, red    - side/ceiling/floor reflect coef -1.0 (perfect elastic)
  SPRING    bounce+kick,   - reflect coef -2.0 (the |coef|>1 is the pinball kick);
            cyan             also floor-bounces (modes 3/4), FUN_2a4a_1349.c:69-88
  WRAP      yellow         - per FUN_2a4a_1349.c side/ceiling DETONATE (see note)
  RANDOM/ERRATIC           - resolved to a concrete 0..5 per round/shot before flight

Per-step force model (RESOLVED, catalog 10 s.2/s.6, FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:44-82),
forward (explicit) Euler in this exact order:

    clamp:   if vx*vx + vy*vy > 1e6:  rescale (vx,vy) to |v| = 1000   (:47-55)
    move:    px += vx*dt ;  py -= vy*dt                               (:62-68)
    drag:    if mode != 1 and visc_mult != 1: vx,vy *= visc_mult      (:72-78)
    gravity: vy -= G_step                                            (:79-80)
    wind:    vx += W_step                                            (:81-82)

The CPU-speed-and-N normalizer `local_a` (FUN_2a4a_01c4.c:29) cancels out of the
trajectory only in the CONTINUOUS (dt->0) limit -- the effective accelerations
below are dt-independent, but the engine integrates with forward Euler, whose
O(dt) truncation does NOT cancel (so the original's landing was machine- and
N-dependent; see constants.PHYSICS_DT's block).  With a fixed step:

    a_gravity = 2500 * GRAVITY  (= 50^2, DAT_5f38_1cf2^2)   vy -= a_gravity*dt
    a_wind    = 1.25 * WIND     (= 50/40, 1cf2/1cf6)        vx += a_wind*dt

The port integrates at the fixed fine PHYSICS_DT (constants.py), realizing the
fast-machine limit where that truncation is negligible and the landing is
N-invariant -- the de-facto canonical behavior all real original hardware sat at.

Screen Y grows downward; py -= vy*dt means vy > 0 is "up".

Launch decomposition (UNBLOCKED via the FP-patched helpers; catalog 10 s.5 had
this BLOCKED but FUN_1000_1204.c:16 is now plainly `fsin` and FUN_1000_13d1.c:14
is `fcos`):

    FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:28   local_a = angle_deg * DAT_5f38_1d08   (deg->rad = pi/180)
    FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:60   FUN_1000_1204(local_a)  -> sin(angle) in ST0
    FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:63   ST0 = power * sin(angle)              -> vy   (param_3 = power)
    FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:65   FUN_1000_13d1(local_a)  -> cos(angle) in ST0
    FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:68   ST0 = power * cos(angle)              -> vx
    caller FUN_38b5_1102.c:56-57: param_3 = tank+0x9e (power),
           param_4 = (win? angle : 180-angle) in degrees.

So the engine form is vx = power*cos(rad), vy = power*sin(rad), power used RAW
(no engine-side power scale).  The absolute px/s scale on screen is set by the
per-shot dt in FUN_2a4a_01c4.c, which is computed from a runtime BogoMIPS probe
(FUN_2a4a_00c3) -> the original had NO fixed frame/step-rate target and its
absolute speed was machine-dependent (full timing model + byte cites in
constants.DT's block).  The trajectory SHAPE is dt-invariant in the continuous
limit (a_grav = 2500*g is dt-free; the integrator is forward Euler so smaller dt
just reduces O(dt) truncation), so the fixed-dt port carries the px/s magnitude
in the calibrated POWER_SCALE; the decomposition FORM above is the recovered
ground truth.
"""
import math

from . import constants as C
from . import guidance
from .objects import Projectile

# deg->rad, DAT_5f38_1d08 on the firing path / DAT_5f38_6100 = 0.017453293 on the
# arc-preview path (byte-confirmed, catalogs/fp_constant_table.log:144).
DEG2RAD = 0.017453293

TURRET_LEN = 12.0

# Boundary-handler return codes (mirror of FUN_2a4a_1349's effect on the
# integrator's DAT_5f38_ce98 / DAT_5f38_ce9a state machine).
_NONE = 0       # no boundary crossed this step (ce9a == 0, ce98 == 0)
_WALL_X = 1     # reflected off a side wall (sets ce9a = 1)  -> vx *= coef
_WALL_Y = 2     # reflected off ceiling/floor (sets ce9a = 2) -> vy *= coef
_DIE = 3        # absorbed / detonated (sets ce98 = 1)        -> remove from flight


def launch(tank, cfg, weapon, power=None, angle=None):
    """Build the projectile leaving `tank`'s muzzle (spawn FUN_2a4a_0763).

    Velocity decomposition per FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:28-68 (UNBLOCKED, see module
    docstring): rad = angle_deg * DEG2RAD; vx = v*cos(rad), vy = v*sin(rad),
    with vy > 0 = up.  `v = power * POWER_SCALE`: the engine uses power raw and
    folds the px/s scale into the MIPS-adaptive dt (FUN_2a4a_01c4.c) which is
    not statically pinned; the browser port carries it in POWER_SCALE.

    FUN_2a4a_0763.c:46-47 seeds px/py (obj+0x14/+0x1c) from the integer launch
    coords param_6/param_7; obj+0x32 bounce energy seeded 0.8 (line 86,
    DAT_5f38_1d24); obj+0x30 bounce counter zeroed (line 87).
    """
    if angle is None:
        angle = tank.angle
    # Ballistic guidance acts at LAUNCH: keep the angle, solve the POWER for the
    # chosen target (DOC L1300, catalog 02 A.2).  Only when the caller did not
    # already supply an explicit power (e.g. a pre-solved game hook passing the
    # wind-corrected guidance.solve_ballistic_power result).  The in-launch solve
    # is drag/wind-free (launch has no world dims); the game hook supplies the
    # wind-corrected refinement.  See guidance.py module note.
    if power is None and getattr(tank, "selected_guidance", None) == 34 \
            and weapon.behavior not in guidance._IGNORES_GUIDANCE:
        solved = guidance.solve_ballistic_power_launch(cfg, tank, weapon)
        if solved is not None:
            power = solved
    if power is None:
        power = tank.power
    rad = angle * DEG2RAD                      # FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:28 angle*DAT_5f38_1d08
    cos_a, sin_a = math.cos(rad), math.sin(rad)
    pivot_x = tank.x
    pivot_y = tank.y - 4
    px = pivot_x + cos_a * TURRET_LEN
    py = pivot_y - sin_a * TURRET_LEN
    v = power * C.POWER_SCALE
    vx = v * cos_a                             # FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:68 power*cos -> vx (+0x04)
    vy = v * sin_a                             # FUN_2a4a_02f2.c:63 power*sin -> vy (+0x0c)
    proj = Projectile(tank, weapon, px, py, vx, vy)
    # Install the +0x4c guidance predicate (FUN_2a4a_0763.c:99-110 analog):
    # reads tank.selected_guidance + guidance_target/_pt, builds proj.guidance.
    # Returns None (no guidance) for unguided shots and guidance-ignoring weapons.
    guidance.attach(tank, cfg, weapon, proj)
    return proj


def step(proj, cfg, dt=C.PHYSICS_DT, tanks=None):
    """One forward-Euler step, listing-order from FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:44-82.

    Order is load-bearing (catalog 10 s.3): position uses the velocity carried
    from the previous step (explicit Euler), then drag, then gravity/wind update
    velocity for the next step.

    `tanks` (optional, keyword) is the live tank list forwarded to the guidance
    predicate so Heat can scan for the nearest enemy in range.  All existing
    positional callers (game._step_flight, ai._simulate_landing) are unaffected;
    they pass no tanks and Heat is simply inert for them.  See guidance.py GAME
    HOOK note for the 1-line game change that supplies it.
    """
    proj.prev_px, proj.prev_py = proj.px, proj.py

    # Step 0: guidance predicate (+0x4c).  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:40-46 fires it BEFORE
    # the clamp/move; it steers vx/vy in place and returns nonzero to stay live.
    if proj.guidance is not None:
        guidance.apply(proj, cfg, tanks=tanks)

    # Step A: velocity-magnitude clamp.  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:44-55.
    #   local_a = vy*vy + vx*vx ; if (DAT_5f38_1d2c=1e6) < local_a:
    #   v /= (speed / DAT_5f38_1d30) where 1d30 = 1000.  Speed-helper is
    #   FUN_1000_0fc8 (sqrt magnitude).  v /= (sp/1000) == v * (1000/sp).
    sp2 = proj.vx * proj.vx + proj.vy * proj.vy
    if sp2 > C.SPEED_CLAMP_SQ:
        sp = math.sqrt(sp2)
        proj.vx = proj.vx / (sp / C.SPEED_CLAMP)
        proj.vy = proj.vy / (sp / C.SPEED_CLAMP)

    # Step B: position integration.  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:62-68.
    #   px += vx*dt ; py -= vy*dt   (dt = DAT_5f38_ceac).  Pre-bounce velocity is
    #   saved to DAT_5f38_e4dc/e4e4 (lines 70-71) -> proj.saved_vx/vy below.
    proj.px += proj.vx * dt
    proj.py -= proj.vy * dt
    proj.saved_vx = proj.vx                    # DAT_5f38_e4dc (FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:70)
    proj.saved_vy = proj.vy                    # DAT_5f38_e4e4 (FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:71)

    # Step C: air viscosity (multiplicative drag).  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:72-78.
    #   Only when obj mode (+0x4a) != 1 AND DAT_5f38_5178 != 1.0.
    vm = cfg.viscosity_mult
    if proj.mode != 1 and vm != 1.0:
        proj.vx *= vm
        proj.vy *= vm

    # Step D: gravity then wind, applied to velocity.  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:79-82.
    #   (still inside the mode != 1 guard) vy -= DAT_5f38_ce9c ; vx += DAT_5f38_cea4.
    #   Effective accelerations with the dt-cancellation (catalog 10 s.4):
    #   ce9c == a_grav*dt, cea4 == a_wind*dt.
    if proj.mode != 1:
        a_grav = C.EFF_GRAVITY_FACTOR * cfg.GRAVITY
        proj.vy -= a_grav * dt
        if cfg.wind:
            a_wind = C.EFF_WIND_FACTOR * cfg.wind
            proj.vx += a_wind * dt

    # round px,py -> integer screen coords (FUN_1000_14df ROUND).  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:86-91.
    proj.sx = int(round(proj.px))
    proj.sy = int(round(proj.py))


def apogee_reached(proj):
    """Y-velocity at/over apogee (vy <= 0).  MIRV/Death's Head split trigger.

    game.py latches the crossing with `prev_vy > 0 >= proj.vy`; this predicate
    is kept for callers that test the post-step sign directly.
    """
    return proj.vy <= 0.0


def handle_walls(proj, cfg, w, h):
    """Reflect / wrap / absorb at the field edges - port of FUN_2a4a_1349
    (boundary detect + reposition) composed with FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:107-160
    (restitution-coefficient selection and application).

    Live wall sub-mode is DAT_5f38_5154 (cfg.live_elastic), one of
    NONE/CONCRETE/PADDED/RUBBER/SPRING/WRAP/RANDOM/ERRATIC (0..7); RANDOM/ERRATIC
    are resolved to a concrete 0..5 mode per round/shot (catalog 13 s.0,
    FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:197-198) so by the time a projectile is in flight
    live_elastic is already in 0..5.

    Returns False when the projectile leaves the tracked field or detonates
    against a boundary (mirror of DAT_5f38_ce98 == 1 -> FUN_2a4a_2228 / off-field
    EDGES_EXTEND track-out); True when it stays in flight (possibly after a
    bounce that mutated px/py/vx/vy in place).
    """
    mode = cfg.live_elastic if hasattr(cfg, "live_elastic") else cfg.elastic
    ext = cfg.EDGES_EXTEND
    x, y = proj.px, proj.py

    # --- boundary detection (FUN_2a4a_1349.c:19-88) --------------------------
    # Field bounds: DAT_5f38_ef42 = left, ef3c = right, ef40 = ceiling (top),
    # ef38 = floor (bottom).  Here those are 0, w-1, 0, h-1 respectively.
    left, right, ceil_y, floor_y = 0.0, float(w - 1), 0.0, float(h - 1)
    code = _NONE
    reflect_to = None        # snapped screen coord for the reflected axis

    # Side walls.  FUN_2a4a_1349.c:19-50.
    if x < left or x > right:
        if mode == 0:                          # NONE: only die once past EDGES_EXTEND
            # FUN_2a4a_1349.c:44 gate is (x < ef42 - 513e) || (ef3c + 513e < x).
            # ef42 = left = 0, ef3c = right = w-1, 513e = EDGES_EXTEND.  Use the
            # binary's bounds exactly (right edge is w-1, not w).
            if x < left - ext or x > right + ext:
                return False                   # (catalog: NONE = fly off, tracked to ext)
            return True
        if mode == 5:                          # WRAP: side wall -> DETONATE (FUN_2a4a_2228)
            # GROUND TRUTH FUN_2a4a_1349.c:21-26: live mode 5 at a side wall calls
            # FUN_2a4a_2228 (detonation dispatch) and sets ce98=1.  The catalog 07
            # paraphrase ("wrap to other edge") is contradicted by these bytes; the
            # airborne projectile detonates, it does not wrap.  See module notes.
            return False
        # CONCRETE/PADDED/RUBBER/SPRING (1..4): reflect off the side wall (ce9a = 1).
        code = _WALL_X
        if mode == 1:
            # CONCRETE snaps to the OPPOSITE edge column, byte-exact
            # FUN_2a4a_1349.c:27-33: iVar3 = ef42; if (x < ef42) iVar3 = ef3c;
            # i.e. left-exit -> snap to RIGHT (ef3c), right-exit -> snap to LEFT
            # (ef42).  The snapped column is then written back as px in
            # FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:147-150 and the struck-axis velocity is scaled by the
            # CONCRETE coef -2.0 (DAT_5f38_1d44).  NOTE: the v1.5 manual (SCORCH.DOC
            # L1924 "CONCRETE walls will block shots from going off screen") describes
            # a block; the shipped bytes instead reposition to the far edge then
            # reverse-and-double vx.  Bytes are authoritative here; the manual prose
            # diverges.  (Mode 5 WRAP, the documented wrap, detonates per :21-26.)
            reflect_to = right if x < left else left
        else:
            # PADDED/RUBBER/SPRING snap to the SAME edge column, FUN_2a4a_1349.c:34-40:
            # iVar3 = ef3c; if (x < ef42) iVar3 = ef42;  i.e. left-exit -> ef42,
            # right-exit -> ef3c.
            reflect_to = left if x < left else right

    # Ceiling.  FUN_2a4a_1349.c:51-68.  Only modes != 0 and != 1 bounce; CONCRETE
    # (1) and NONE (0) do not reflect off the ceiling here.
    elif y < ceil_y:
        if mode == 0 or mode == 1:
            # NONE/CONCRETE: ceiling is not a reflector in 1349; for NONE the shell
            # simply continues (it will only die past the side EDGES_EXTEND or on
            # terrain).  Keep it in flight; clamp the screen coord like _1f5a.
            return True
        if mode == 5:                          # WRAP ceiling -> detonate (1349:53-58)
            return False
        code = _WALL_Y
        reflect_to = ceil_y

    # Floor.  FUN_2a4a_1349.c:69-88.  Only RUBBER (3) and SPRING (4) bounce off
    # the floor; everything else detonates.
    elif y >= floor_y:
        if mode == 3 or mode == 4:             # RUBBER / SPRING floor bounce
            # Slow-bounce floor STOP, byte-exact (FUN_2a4a_1349:148f-14b9,
            # RECOVERED_MISC.md T2): a RUBBER/SPRING shell on the floor row whose
            # pre-bounce vertical velocity is in the band -50 < vy < 50 STOPS
            # (detonates) rather than bouncing.  1d4c=-50.0 (f64), 1cf2=50.0 (f32),
            # e4e4=pre-bounce vy.  The band is symmetric, so the port's vy sign
            # convention does not matter.
            if -50.0 < proj.vy < 50.0:
                return False                   # detonate: too slow to keep bouncing
            code = _WALL_Y
            reflect_to = floor_y
        else:
            return False                       # detonate on floor (FUN_2a4a_2228)

    if code == _NONE:
        return True

    # --- restitution coefficient + apply (FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:120-159) -----------
    proj.bounce_count += 1                      # obj+0x30 ++ (FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:121-122)

    # Coefficient by live wall mode, FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:123-132 (with DAT_5f38_1c7a
    # == 0, which holds for plain field-edge bounces; the 1c7a != 0 branch at
    # :134-138 is the SHIELD-DEFLECT path armed by FUN_2a4a_2487 on a deflector-
    # shield hit, not a field edge, so it is out of handle_walls' scope):
    #   RUBBER(3) -> DAT_5f38_1d34 = -1.0
    #   PADDED(2) -> DAT_5f38_1d3c = -0.5
    #   default (CONCRETE 1 / SPRING 4 / other) -> DAT_5f38_1d44 = -2.0
    # SPRING(4) takes the default -2.0: that >1 magnitude IS the "pinball kick"
    # the manual describes (catalogs/04_menus_ui.md:414); SPRING is not a saved-
    # velocity restore.
    if mode == 3:
        coef = C.WALL_COEF["RUBBER"]            # DAT_5f38_1d34 = -1.0
    elif mode == 2:
        coef = C.WALL_COEF["PADDED"]            # DAT_5f38_1d3c = -0.5
    else:
        coef = C.WALL_COEF["DEFAULT"]           # DAT_5f38_1d44 = -2.0

    # Bounce-energy decay after the 6th bounce.  FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:141-145:
    #   if (obj+0x30 > 6) { coef *= obj+0x32 ; obj+0x32 *= DAT_5f38_1d24 (=0.8) }
    if proj.bounce_count > 6:
        coef *= proj.bounce_energy
        proj.bounce_energy *= C.BOUNCE_ENERGY

    # Reposition to the wall, then scale the struck-axis velocity by coef.
    # FUN_2a4a_0b1f.c:147-159 writes px/py back from the snapped integer screen
    # coords (&DAT_5f38_e34a / e412) and multiplies vx (ce9a==1) or vy (ce9a==2).
    if code == _WALL_X:
        proj.px = reflect_to
        proj.vx *= coef
    else:                                       # _WALL_Y
        proj.py = reflect_to
        proj.vy *= coef

    proj.sx = int(round(proj.px))
    proj.sy = int(round(proj.py))
    return True

"""Command parser — id-based, reproducing the original's whole-word matching.

The original upper-cases the line, wraps it in spaces, and for each vocab token does a
`strstr` of the space-bracketed word inside the space-bracketed input, returning the id
of the first matching token (verbs and nouns are separate 1-based id spaces; synonyms
share an id). `FUN_16a8_1048`. Numeric arguments (TOETS/DRAAI/BEL/KOOP) are the digit
run in the line.
"""
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

from .world import World


@dataclass
class Cmd:
    raw: str
    verb: int = 0          # verb id (0 = none/unknown)
    noun: int = 0          # noun id (0 = none)
    number: Optional[str] = None


class Parser:
    def __init__(self, world: World):
        self.verbs = world.verbs
        self.nouns = world.nouns

    def parse(self, line: str) -> Cmd:
        up = " " + re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line.strip().upper()) + " "
        verb = 0
        for v in self.verbs:                       # id order; first token match wins
            if any((" " + w + " ") in up for w in v["words"]):
                verb = v["id"]; break
        noun = 0
        for n in self.nouns:
            if any((" " + w + " ") in up for w in n["words"]):
                noun = n["id"]; break
        m = re.search(r"[0-9][0-9\-]*", up)
        return Cmd(raw=line, verb=verb, noun=noun, number=(m.group(0) if m else None))

# MinerVGA reverse-engineering notes

Evidence ledger for the source rebuild in `port/`. "Observed" means read from the
shipped bytes, the listing or the data files; "inferred" means deduced from usage.
Regenerate the analysis artifacts with `re/decompile.ps1` (output in `re/out/`).

## Target and tooling

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Release | MinerVGA 1.1, 10 Sep 1989, public domain, FrodoSoft (H. W. Stiles). MS QuickBASIC 4.0, SCREEN 12 |
| `MINERVGA.EXE` | DOS MZ, 109,231 bytes, sha256 `b373b2730b694ecd78a37368fc9e6a3ed25d39a43a77365dcaa69e8adeef11c2` |
| Packing | Microsoft EXEPACK (`Packed file is corrupt` stub). `re/tools/unexepack.py`: real CS:IP 0846:0010, SS:SP 1CBB:0800, 1,813 relocations |
| FP emulation | 8087 emulator interrupts INT 34h–3Dh in the BASIC module (2,920 sites). `re/tools/unemu87.py` rewrites them to x87 opcodes (FIxRQQ/FJxRQQ mapping) |
| Decompiler | Ghidra 12.1.4 headless (`ExportDecompilation.java`, `ExportListing.java`), JDK 21 |
| REA | REA 6.4.0 `inspect-artifact` identified the target as `dos-mz` (Evidence `ev_8019655f…`). Deep native analysis was not possible on this host: REA's Windows Ghidra provider accepts PE only ("DOS MZ/COM analysis requires the Ghidra 16-bit real-mode adapter") and no WSL distro was installed, so Ghidra was driven directly |
| Compiler for the port | QB64 Phoenix Edition 4.6.0 (win-x64 7z sha256 `2c18a41a1435248b14b2080404811e9c6f7c0ac6d9e41976f720544480729e61`). 4.7.0-GLFW was available but had just switched windowing backend |

## Memory map (load image, Ghidra segment = 1000h + paragraph)

| Segment | Image offset | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 0x0000 | The compiled BASIC module: one module-level program, GOSUB routines, `1000:0030`–`~845f` |
| 1846 | 0x8460 | C start-up and x87 helpers: `041d` compare, `03d8` to INTEGER (round half even), `0433` FIX, `0449` INT (floor), `03c4` INTEGER→SINGLE |
| 1942 | 0x9420 | QuickBASIC 4.0 runtime (BCOM40) |
| 2683 | 0x16830 | DGROUP: variables from DS:0000, constants from DS:2A40, DATA records from DS:4830 |

## Runtime entry points (1942:xxxx)

Observed call sites, names inferred from argument patterns and context.

| Address | Statement | | Address | Statement |

| 854a | SCREEN | | 9d5c | INKEY$ |

| 97ef / 97f4 | PRINT string `;` / newline | | 7464 | VAL |
| 97d1 / 97d6 | PRINT SINGLE `;` / newline | | a27e | STR$ |
| 97b3 | PRINT integer | | 9ddd / 9da4 / 9e1a | concatenate / assign / compare strings |
| 9b61 | PRINT USING | | a04d, a11a, a0f6, a103 | LEN, MID$, LEFT$, RIGHT$ |

| 1a00 | LINE | | 5820 / 6040 | OPEN / CLOSE |

`L_6800` pushes `16,24,527,455, 0, -1, -1`: the final −1 is the SCREEN flag (1852 skips the
relative-origin setup), so interior screens use absolute coordinates.

## Routines (GOSUB labels = code addresses)

| Label | Role | Port file |
|---|---|---|
| main 0030–07c4 | start-up, first screen, main loop | `MINERVGA.BAS` |
| L_0165 / L_01a3 | DEF FN max / min (`MXR`, `MNR`) | `view.bi` |

| L_1daa, L_200f, L_24e1, L_2de2 | arrive/reveal, resolve cell, cell effects + dig cost, spring/cave-in | `mine.bi` |

| L_5d23 / L_5fce | save / restore | `screens.bi` |
| L_5831, L_6623, L_6823, L_6e11, L_7537, L_79c1, L_8310 | help, doors, store, bank, hospital, saloon, rumour | `buildings.bi` |
| L_6800 | play-area clear (`VIEW SCREEN ... ,0 : VIEW`) | `view.bi` |

## Variables

All original variables are module-level. Role names and DS addresses are listed in
`docs/porting-conventions.md`; everything else is named `V` + DS address. Arrays:

| Array | DS | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `M%(c, r)` | 003A | INTEGER (0..40, 0..120), column-major (`0x3A + 2*(c + 41*r)`); ends at 0x26FC |
| `INV%(i)` | 26FC | INTEGER (0..12): slot i holds the item's sprite number or 0 |
| `MSGL$(i)`, `MSGC(i)` | 2716, 2746 | (0..11); lines 1..10 shown, 11 is the always-empty source of the scroll |
| `HSCORE`, `HNAME$`, `HFLAG` | 292C, 2960, 2994 | (0..12) |

Inventory slots: 1 shovel (3), 2 pick (4), 3 drill (5), 4 lantern (6), 5 bucket (7), 6 torch (8),
7 dynamite (9), 8 ring (52), 9 condom (50), 10 diamond (51), 11 pump (49), 12 clover (2).

## File formats (observed)

- **`MINERVGA.LBR`**: header `"MINER-VGASpritesLibrary",53` (53 = last index, so 54 sprites), then
  per sprite `idx,"name",16,24,<97 ints>,`. Each sprite is a QuickBASIC GET array: width,
  height, then per row four 2-byte planes (B, G, R, I), MSB = leftmost pixel. Cell value = sprite index.
- **`MINERVGA.SAV`**: line 0 = PT, AU, AG, BANK, HEALTH, X, Y, OFFX, SHAFT, LIGHT, TOOLS, TORCHT,
  LANTERNT; line 1 = `INV%(1..12)`; then 113 lines of `M%(1..39, r)` for r = 6..118. OFFY and the
  elevator position are not saved (saving is only allowed in town). The shipped file has no spaces
  and ends in ^Z; the game itself writes with `PRINT #`.
- **`MINERVGA.SCR`**: 10 lines `score ,"name", flag` (flag 1 = won).

## Random numbers (observed in the runtime)

`RND`: `seed = (seed * &HFD43FD + &HC39EC3) AND &HFFFFFF`, result `seed / 2^24`, initial seed
`&H050000` (DS:59D3). The runtime (1942:9ea7) multiplies in 16-bit pieces using the words at
DS:6372 (`43FD`) and DS:6376 (`9EC3`) plus their low bytes for bits 16–23; read as one dword
those words look like `&H343FD` / `&H269EC3`, which is wrong. Verified: the mine in a DOSBox-X
capture of the original (clock pinned to :30) is reproduced exactly, and an exhaustive search of
all 2^24 states finds only the predicted one. `RANDOMIZE n`: n as a DOUBLE, word 2 XOR word 3 replaces seed bits 8–23.
The constants equal QBasic/QB 4.5's. The port still uses its own `QRND`/`QRandomize`
(`port/platform.bi`) so seeding and RND(0) behave exactly as the original's runtime. `QRND` returns DOUBLE because the original computed `INT(RND * n)` in x87
extended precision.

Seeding: the title does `RANDOMIZE VAL(MID$(TIME$, 7, 2)) * 10` (60 possible mines); every cell
reveal re-seeds with `VAL(seconds) + CC + RR`.

## Rules (observed)

- **Mine generation:** r = 6..118, c = 1..39: `INT(RND*4)+10`, a 13 is re-rolled as `INT(RND*2)+10`.
  Column 40 = shaft (16). Fixed: M(40,3)=40, M(40,4)=17, M(40,5)=38, M(1,118)=53.
- **Cell resolve (L_200f):** v = `INT(RND*1040) + X - 39 - Y` (player position). v > 810 sandstone 47,
  > 570 granite 14, > 400 volcanic 48, > 300 cave-in 46, > 240 spring 41, > 70 silver 43, > 30 gold 44,
  > 2 platinum 45, 0..2 clover 2, −2..−1 diamond 51, −4..−3 pump 49, below water 42.
- **Light reveal (L_1daa):** over the 3×3 neighbourhood a 13 resolves if `INT(RND*100)+1 <= LIGHT/10`,
  a 12 becomes 13 if `INT(RND*100)+1 <= LIGHT`. Lantern +20 (timer 2000 keys), torch +10 (1500), clover +20.
- **Dig cost:** factor f by cell (earth 1, sandstone .5, volcanic 1.5, gold 2.5, platinum 5, clover 7);
  `IF TOOLS = 0 THEN f = f*2`; `BANK = BANK - (10 - TOOLS)*f`.
- **Elevator:** descending into row 5 costs $30, `B` jumps to SHAFT for $40, `T` (any column) to row 6.
  Store `V` adds 10 rows (60 ft) for $100 while SHAFT <= 100, so the maximum is 110.
- **Store:** A shovel $100, B pick $150, C drill $250, D lantern $300, E bucket $200, F torch $100,
  G dynamite $300.
- **Bank:** quote base b = `INT(RND*10)+45`; PT `INT(RND*10)+5b`, AU `INT(RND*10)+b`, AG
  `INT(RND*10)+b/5`; payout `INT(q*oz+.5)`; diamond sells for $1000.
- **Lose:** `HEALTH < 0 OR BANK < -100`. **Win:** saloon `A` with the ring and BANK > 20000.

## Preserved quirks

Marked `' QUIRK:` in the source. The port keeps them deliberately.

- `PT = AU = AG = 0` at start-up parses as a comparison (result 0).
- `T` works from any column and teleports to row 6 without changing X.
- The elevator car can go one row past SHAFT (`ELEV <= SHAFT` before moving).
- No funds checks in the store, hospital or saloon; the store fills the INV% slot before the sale.
- Losing the pick does not reduce TOOLS; losing a light does not clear its timer.
- Spring and cave-in cells stay in place and re-trigger; the signature cell 53 charges digging every time.
- Drill/pump "Not Here!" is never shown.
- Dynamite: a stale CC/RR redraw after placing the bomb; `HEALTH - INT(RND*15) + 2` can raise health.
- Hospital `A` charges $10 per point (the sign says $100 per day) and can refund money.
- The saloon's "immediate need of Hospitality!" test is inverted.
- HUD numbers of 5+ digits overflow the frame (classic layout only; the wide HUD has room).

## Port-only changes

- Layout: wide 960×540 (40×20 tiles, whole mine width; HUD panel at text columns 85–120;
  interiors shifted +64 px; full-screen scenes centred at +160,+32) or `/classic` 640×480.
  Vertical scroll in wide mode: down when `Y > OFFY + 17`, up when `Y < OFFY + 4`, steps of 10,
  clamped to 0..98; `B` clamps the same way. Classic keeps the original expressions.
- `OFFX` keeps its original 0/8 logic in both layouts (it is saved), but wide mode draws with 0.
- Busy waits on INKEY$ are frame-limited (`_LIMIT 60`); test hooks `MINERVGA_SCRIPT` / `MINERVGA_TIME`.
- `END` is `SYSTEM` (no "press any key" from QB64).
- The title stays up for 3 s or until a key (loading the sprites used to take that long).
- The window opens at the largest integer multiple of the canvas that fits 90% of the desktop
  (`$RESIZE:STRETCH` + `SetWindowPos`); `Alt+Enter` fullscreen is integer-scaled, unsmoothed.
- Win screen: each PLAY phrase waits until less than 3 s of music is queued (QB 4.0's 32-note
  background buffer blocked the same way) and each firework step calls `Idle`.
- `LINE INPUT` for the high-score name goes through `LineIn$` so test scripts can type it.
  `LineIn$` no longer calls `LINE INPUT` at all: its own loop echoes keys, shows a `_` cursor,
  stops at the right edge and takes gamepad input.
- Gamepad (XInput, `xinput1_4.dll`) in `platform.bi`: presses become the keys the game reads,
  chosen by `VIEWKIND%` (map: actions; building: menu marker; help and scenes: `" "`, which
  no command reacts to). Start on the map opens a pause menu drawn over a copy of the screen,
  which is put back unchanged; it holds the commands that end or reload the game (`S`, `R`,
  `X`) plus `H` and `Q`. Buildings call `PadMenu` around their key loops. No marker or overlay
  is drawn without a pad, so keyboard play is pixel-identical to before.

## Verification against the original

`tools/emu/capture.ps1` runs the original in DOSBox-X (clock pinned with `time 12:00:30`).
With `MINERVGA_TIME` set to the same clock, `/classic` screenshots are pixel-identical for:
the help screen, the generated town and mine (seconds 30, 9 title RND calls), the shipped save
restored, a dig sequence hitting granite (dig second 34/35), and an elevator ride plus three
earth digs (`$850 - $30 - 3 * 8 = $796`). Other paths (minerals, hazards, buildings, scenes) were
exercised with scripted runs of the port in both layouts and checked against the listing.

' MinerVGA 1.1 (1989, public domain, Harrell W. Stiles / FrodoSoft) - source rebuilt
' from the compiled QuickBASIC 4.0 executable for QB64-PE. See docs/porting-conventions.md.
'
' Routine ownership (GOSUB labels are the original code addresses):
'   MINERVGA.BAS  main program and main loop          1000:0030-07c4
'   view.bi       load, town/mine setup, frame, HUD, messages, map view, movement, keys
'   mine.bi       sound effects, digging, hazards, elevator keys, dynamite, drill/pump
'   buildings.bi  help, doors, store, bank, hospital, saloon, rumours
'   screens.bi    title, game end, tombstone, high scores, win, save/restore
'   platform.bi   display layout (wide 960x540 or /classic 640x480), sprites, RND, keyboard/gamepad input

$RESIZE:STRETCH
'$INCLUDE:'platform_decl.bi'
'$INCLUDE:'globals.bi'

InitDataDir
InputInit
GfxInit INSTR(UCASE$(COMMAND$), "/CLASSIC") = 0

' ---- 1000:0030-0164  start-up --------------------------------------------------
' SCREEN 12 is done by GfxInit. 1942:a5a5 (END) is translated as SYSTEM throughout:
' compiled QB 4.0 returned straight to DOS, QB64's END would wait for a key.
LOCATE , , 0
V0036$ = "MINERVGA.LBR" ' sprite library name (LoadSprites opens it via DataPath$)
GOSUB L_07c5 ' title, load sprites
GOSUB L_0923 ' miner figures
X = 35: OLDX = 35
Y = 4: OLDY = 4
OFFX = 8: OFFY = 0
HEALTH = 100
PT = AU = AG = 0 ' QUIRK: parsed as PT = ((AU = AG) = 0), which happens to be 0
BANK = 1500
K$ = "*"
FACE = 1
ELEV = 4
SHAFT = 20
LIGHT = 0
TOOLS = 0
SOUNDON = 1
TORCHT = -1
LANTERNT = -1

' ---- 1000:048e-04bf  first screen ------------------------------------------------
GOSUB L_0bf0 ' frame and HUD
GOSUB L_5831 ' help screen
GOSUB L_0a10 ' town
GOSUB L_0a9c ' mine
GOSUB L_3d5d ' wait for a key
MS$ = "Welcome to; MinerVGA ;": MSCOL = 14: GOSUB L_1496
GOSUB L_1149
GOSUB L_1384

' ---- 1000:04c0-07c4  main loop ---------------------------------------------------
DO WHILE K$ <> "X"
    GOSUB L_3d5d
    IF VAL(K$) > 0 THEN GOSUB L_168d: K$ = "*"
    IF K$ = "E" THEN GOSUB L_6623: K$ = "*"
    IF K$ = "D" OR K$ = "P" THEN GOSUB L_6214
    ' QUIRK: T works from any column; only B requires the elevator column.
    IF K$ = "T" OR K$ = "B" AND X = 40 THEN GOSUB L_3491
    IF K$ = "Q" THEN
        IF SOUNDON = 0 THEN SOUNDON = 1 ELSE SOUNDON = 0
    END IF
    IF K$ = "S" THEN GOSUB L_5d23
    IF K$ = "R" THEN GOSUB L_5fce: K$ = "*"
    IF K$ = "H" THEN
        MS$ = "  Help!!  ;": MSCOL = 10: GOSUB L_1496
        GOSUB L_5831
        GOSUB L_3d5d
        GOSUB L_1149
        GOSUB L_1384
    END IF
    IF K$ = "Y" THEN GOSUB L_3692
    IF HEALTH < 0 OR BANK < -100 THEN GOSUB L_3e49
    IF LANTERNT > 0 THEN LANTERNT = LANTERNT - 1
    IF TORCHT > 0 THEN TORCHT = TORCHT - 1
    IF LANTERNT = 0 THEN
        LANTERNT = LANTERNT - 1

        GOSUB L_1074

        INV%(6) = 0
        LIGHT = LIGHT - 10
        MS$ = "The torch ;is used up;": MSCOL = 4: GOSUB L_1496
        GOSUB L_1074

SYSTEM

# sam - the SDL3 port

One executable, `sam`, that runs Secret Agent episodes 1-3 from the canonical Turbo Pascal source
in [../game/](../game/). Design, memory model and contract: [../docs/port.md](../docs/port.md).

```
game/*.PAS --tools/pas2c.py (per episode, at build time; never committed)--> build/.../port-gen/samN/*.c
sam = generated episodes (s1_/s2_/s3_) + tp/ (System, Crt, Dos) + lib/ (the six assembly objects
      in C) + pc/ (emulated PC: memory, interrupts, BIOS, PIT, speaker, keyboard, game port,
      EGA/VGA, text mode; SDL3 front end) + launcher.c
```

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `pc/pc.h` | the binding platform contract |
| `pc/` | real-mode memory and program placement, far-code registry and IVT, safe-point interrupt scheduler, BIOS (INT 8/9/10h/11h/16h/1Ah/1Ch, used INT 21h services), PIT and PC speaker, keyboard controller, game port timing model, EGA/VGA (planes, latches, offset/start/pel panning/line compare), text mode with a CP437 font derived from GNU Unifont (SIL OFL 1.1, `pc/fonts-LICENSE.txt`, source in `pc/font-source/`), SDL3 window/input/audio/scripts |
| `tp/` | Turbo Pascal 5.0 runtime: `system.c` (strings, sets, heap manager, files, Random, Str/Val, Halt/ExitProc), `crt.c`, `dos.c`; `tp.h` is the generated-code ABI |
| `lib/` | ProGraphx, Genus PCX toolkit, TEXTOUT, JOYSTICK, DECODE and CMOSPIT routines in C (`samlib.h`) |
| `tests/` | platform self-tests, scripted determinism test, boot scripts |
| `launcher.c` | automatic episode discovery, emulated text-mode chooser and direct `--episode 1|2|3` starts |
| `release/` | player README and release notices; `tools/package_port.py` packages an explicit data-free allowlist |

## Build and run

MinGW-w64 gcc 12 (`C:/msys64/mingw64`), CMake 3.20+, SDL3 3.4.16 (`SDL3_ROOT` in CMakeLists.txt).

```bash
cmake -S port -B build/port -G "MinGW Makefiles" -DSAM_OPTIMIZATION=2
```

```bash
cmake --build build/port -j4
```

`sam` finds complete episodes in the executable's directory, independently of the current
working directory. A single installed episode starts immediately; multiple episodes open the
mission chooser. Use arrows and Enter or 1/2/3; S opens port settings and Esc exits. Quitting an
episode to DOS returns to the chooser. Each start reloads emulated memory, DS, devices, handles,
vectors and native assembly-library private state in place, keeping the SDL window. The chooser
uses BIOS text mode and the port's licensed CP437 font, without initializing a game for its UI.

`build/port/sam.exe --episode N --data DIR` runs episode N directly with its data files in DIR,
then exits when the episode ends (SDL3.dll beside the executable or on PATH). A complete episode
requires APO/TTL/CRD, three GFX files, three E.SND files and its END file(s); CFG and the DOS EXE
are not required. See [release/README.txt](release/README.txt) for exact names and controller use.
Options: `--headless`, `--no-audio`, `--script FILE`
(`<ms> key|keydown|keyup NAME`, `<ms> shot FILE.png`, `<ms> quit`), `--realtime-script`,
`--wav FILE`, `--ega`/`--vga`, `--physical-shots`.
Script times span the launcher session; future events are rebased when a DOS load resets the
device clock. Direct-start scripts keep their existing timing and captures.

Alt+Enter and F11 toggle fullscreen. Keyboard repeat remains the
PC's 500 ms delay / 30 Hz repeat. Controller left stick/D-pad and South/West buttons use the
emulated game port's X/Y and buttons 0/1 (jump/fire); enable/calibrate Joystick in the game's
options. No controller event edits game state or generates keyboard input.

Presentation settings are `sam.json` **beside the executable**, separate from the game's
`SAMn.CFG`. The chooser offers fullscreen, integer scaling versus aspect-correct fit, optional
smooth filtering, overscan border and window sizes; resizing also saves the windowed size. Defaults
retain integer/aspect presentation and nearest filtering; the overscan border is cropped. CLI overrides:
`--fullscreen` / `--windowed`, `--scaling integer|fit`, `--smooth` / `--no-smooth`,
`--border` / `--no-border`, `--window-size WIDTHxHEIGHT`, `--settings FILE`.
The latter changes only the host settings path.
Use a writable directory for persistence; read-only locations report a save error and keep
playing. Malformed settings fall back to defaults. These options never change DOS scanout or
the source-frame screenshots, so the existing boot hashes remain unchanged.

Build a Windows release with `python tools/package_port.py`. It produces
`build/releases/sam-windows-x64.zip` containing only sam.exe, SDL3.dll and the player README and
SDL/font notices. No original data, CFG, saves, scripts or test outputs enter the archive.
`python -B tools/check_package.py --window` unpacks into fresh test folders, copies original data
there, and checks discovery, all three titles, auto-starts, settings persistence and four normal
episode quits/restarts, plus a visible window. Captures are disposable test outputs.

Linux source builds use the same CMake command with the system compiler, make/Ninja and an
SDL3 CMake package, without MinGW arguments. Linux execution was not tested here: WSL refuses
distribution enumeration with E_ACCESSDENIED. Windows-specific source calls are guarded by
`_WIN32`; packaging the Windows zip requires a Windows build.

Windows real-time play uses a D3D11 flip presenter on a separate thread, with vsync and one
pending frame. It displays the latest completed emulated scanout and replaces intermediate
frames when the monitor is slower than the emulated 70.0863 Hz display. A static frame remains in
the compositor without repeated rendering. Vsync, GPU work and resizing never hold the PC
thread or its timer interrupts; SDL window events and input stay on the main thread. This
backend requires Windows 10 version 1803 or later and a D3D11-capable graphics driver. Other
platforms retain the SDL renderer. Scaling, borders, fullscreen and filtering use the same
presentation settings. Manual-clock scripts retain their existing rendering and timing.

Host input pumping runs at most once per millisecond during productive work, and before every
blocking wait. Windows keyboard/window messages wake those waits immediately; an attached
controller bounds them to one millisecond. Hardware retrace loops can identify their requested
status-bit edge through `pc_wait_video_status`, without changing any returned port value. The
Windows wait uses a high-resolution waitable timer. Emulated time stops exactly at the next
device edge, so an oversleep cannot hide the retrace pulse; no precision busy spin is needed.
Later waits catch up against wall time, with lag beyond 100 ms rebasing wall pacing without
skipping PC history. Productive work samples elapsed wall time at safe points while preserving
pending device edges. The PIT and virtual display remain independent of host presentation.

Speaker playback uses the audio device's native rate to avoid resampling and a 10 ms replay
margin (previously 40 ms). Playback follows the emulated clock and holds the current PIT tone
during a host stall. The requested device period is 256 frames; the actual period is
device-dependent. WAV capture remains deterministic at 44.1 kHz. Opt-in `SAM_HOST_METRICS=FILE`
writes cumulative wall-time diagnostics once per second: safe points, event pumps, sleeps,
scanouts, presentations, audio work and late audible speaker changes. `tools/measure_host.py`
measures total process CPU as a percentage of one core in real-time title/menu/gameplay/fade
scripts; `tools/check_host.py` checks visible presentation and an intentionally stalled
presenter against the unchanged boot images and IRQ counts. `host_latency` measures an SDL
event reaching the BIOS keyboard ring while the PC is blocked.
`SAM_DIAG_FLIPS=FILE` logs each CRTC start-address high-byte write with emulated and host time;
`tools/check_timing.py FILE --start 10 --end 22` summarizes its cadence, including loading gaps.
The raw-port `clock_edges` regression inserts host stalls longer than the retrace pulse and
checks that every pulse and the PIT remain observable without a library wait hint.

`SAM_DIAG_SCANOUT=FILE` logs the start address and fine pan used at each composed frame,
with stride and effective X/Y. `python tools/check_scroll.py --exe build/port/sam.exe`
checks every frame during scripted mission walking in both directions and title/credits
vertical panning, on VGA and EGA. It copies disposable episode data without the player's CFG.
The `scanout_latches` CTest checks writes on both sides of sync and raw register reads.

No DOS tools are needed: each episode's memory placement (PSP, DS, SS, heap) comes from
[../config/port.json](../config/port.json); DATA offsets are computed by the translator. With the DOS
toolchain present, `tools/pas2c_placement_check.py` recomputes the placement from the reference
build and requires equality.

## Checks

`python tools/validate.py --port` (or `python -B tools/pas2c_check.py --integration`): DS layout
and record sizes against the originals, generated C for all three episodes, the semantic corpus
(`tests/port/semantics/`) against the real TP 5.0, platform CTest, and SAM1-3 booted headless to
their title screens at -O0 and -O2.

`lib/` against the assembled originals (needs the DOS reference builds,
`python tools/verify.py --episodes sam1,sam2,sam3 --keep`): `python -B tools/libdiff.py --matrix`
runs every routine the game calls (200 random + 16 realistic cases each; memory, EGA state,
ports, BIOS/DOS calls compared under the rules documented at the top of `tools/libdiff.py`),
`--screens` decodes all screen files through both
display paths, `tools/callsite_report.py` lists the call sites whose AX the C routines derive from
arguments.

## Status

* Milestones 1-5 reached: all three episodes run; the library differential gate covers all 43
  called routines and all 13 screens; strict lockstep against the original passes for 18
  scenarios of SAM1-3 (`python tools/validate.py --lockstep`); automatic launcher, presentation
  settings and the Windows release package.
* Open: Linux execution testing, ending-screen gameplay coverage. Android is deferred.

The optional `-DSAM_LOCKSTEP=ON` target and `tools/lockstep.py` run the original in Unicorn on
this port's PC model and compare it with the port at every gameplay frame. Usage,
synchronization, comparisons and the named rules (including the documented uninitialised
sound-priority difference) are in [tests/port/lockstep/README.md](../tests/port/lockstep/README.md).

moledesign-championsofkrynn-docs-changes.text:
# Changes from the original

What the remake does differently from the 1990 Amiga game, and why. It has
three parts:

* **Improvements**: deliberate changes to fix the original's flaws.
* **Rule choices**: where the remake had to pick a rule or a number. The
  table says where to change each one.
* **Bugs fixed**: problems found and fixed while rebuilding the engine.

The story, the maps, the event scripts, the monsters and the items are all
the original's: the remake reads them from your own disks.

## Improvements

### Presentation

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| 320x200 screen, everything at one size | Laid out for 1920x1080. Art is enlarged by whole numbers (3D view 7x, big pictures 5x, combat 2x) so it stays crisp, and text is drawn at full resolution. Any window size works (letterboxed); F11 for full screen. |
| | Mouse works in menus, combat and every screen. |
| | An automap of the squares you have visited is always on screen. |
| Journal entries and tavern tales printed in the manual ("read journal entry 51") | The entry opens on screen when the story mentions it, maps and pictures included. Every entry found is kept in a Journal (J), with Journal and Tavern tabs. |

### Combat

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| A fake isometric battlefield: a skewed grid drawn from the same tiles | A straight top-down grid built from the map around the party, or open ground outdoors, using the original icons and tiles. |
| Hard to tell how far you can move or what is threatened | Squares you can reach are lit, squares enemies threaten are marked, and the panel shows your hit chance and damage against the target. |
| Area spells aimed blind | Before you cast, the squares a spell covers are lit, every creature it will hit is outlined, and you are warned if friends are inside a Fireball or Stinking Cloud. |
| Swapping between bow and sword by hand | A bow stays slung beside a melee weapon; F shoots, moving into an enemy strikes. |
| Wands and potions had to be readied, and an unidentified one could not be told apart | I lists every usable item with its power and charges; nothing needs readying first. |
| Arrows spent | After a victory the party recovers half its arrows and quarrels and every thrown dart and javelin. |
| Monsters fight to the last goblin | Monsters check morale and may break and run (see Rule choices). |
| Playing every character every round | U hands a character to the computer; shift+U the whole party. |
| Walls drawn only from the original art | Every wall, door, floor and obstacle has a fixed id (`W1-01-03`, `O-WILD-06`...). Put `remake/art/blocks/<ID>.png` in place to redraw one ([art/README.md](../remake/art/README.md), [BLOCKS.md](../remake/art/BLOCKS.md)). |

### Camping and spells

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| Slow natural healing: many rests, each a chance of being ambushed | A night heals 1 hit point per character level. "Rest until healed" rests as many nights as needed in one go and stops if a night is interrupted. |
| Healing the party meant casting each cure spell by hand, resting, and repeating | Fix: the clerics cast all their cures on whoever is most hurt, then the party rests and repeats until everyone is whole. |
| Interruptions checked repeatedly through a rest | Checked once a night, with each map's own chance (see Rule choices). |
| Unclear why a mage has more spells some nights | The memorise screen shows every slot by level, the moon bonus, and the phase of each moon. |

### Money and items

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| Coins carried by each character in seven kinds; pooling and sharing by hand | One purse for the whole party. It pays in steel and makes its own change, using the cheapest coins first. |
| Treasure split by hand through Take / Pool / Share menus | Coins go straight into the purse; you choose who carries each item, or press A to take all. |
| Selling gems and jewelry one at a time | J sells all gems and jewelry in one go. |

### Training

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| A character who earned two levels between visits to a hall lost the experience beyond the first | Nothing is lost: each Train goes up one level per class, and the character can train again at once if the experience is there. |
| Hit points for a new level rolled from scratch (a fighter could gain 1) | A new level never gives less than half the hit die, plus constitution. |
| Who can train, and how far off the others are, found by trying | The hall lists every character's classes, experience and the next level's figure, and marks who is ready. |

### Characters

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| One roll of the abilities per try | 4d6 best three, inside the race's ranges, rolled again as often as you like; the screen shows which class minimums a roll misses. |
| A new character's hit points could be 1 per die | At least half of each hit die. |
| Party management only at a hall's menus | The same at a hall (C new, R remove), plus `--new` to start the story with a new party. |

### Saving

| Original | Remake |
|----------|--------|
| Saving only from the camp menu, to a save disk | F5 saves into one of ten slots (A-J) whenever the party is free to move; F9 loads, also after the party falls. `krynn.py --load A` starts from a save. Saves are written so a crash cannot leave a half-written file. |

## Rule choices

The original engine's code for these has not been fully decoded yet, so the
remake follows the manual and AD&D. Each one is in a single place and easy
to change.

| What | Remake's rule | Where |
|------|---------------|-------|
| Natural healing | 1 HP per character level per 8-hour night | `World.night` in `remake/kroc/world.py` |
| Rest interruptions | Each map's `precamp` script sets the chance (`7ED3`); rolled once per night | `World.camp` in `world.py` |
| Spell slots | Krynn's tables (manual pp.57-58: White and Red Robes, clerics of good and of neutral gods, knights of the Sword and Rose), the cleric's wisdom bonus, the moons (p.16). This reproduces the saved party's spells exactly. | `SLOTS` in `remake/kroc/magic.py` |
| Experience and levels | The manual's advancement tables and level limits (pp.56-58). Multi-class characters share earned experience between their classes. | `remake/kroc/training.py` |
| THAC0 by level | AD&D first-edition matrices (fighters improve every 2 levels, clerics every 3, thieves 4, mages 5); matches every saved character | `training.thac0_for` |
| Hit points per level | One hit die by class (fighters and knights d10, rangers and clerics d8, thieves d6, mages d4), at least half the die, plus constitution (manual p.55); shared out for multi-class characters | `training.roll_hp` |
| Item powers | Wands: Magic Missiles (2 missiles), Fireballs, Lightning, Ice Storm, Paralyzation (Hold, up to 3) cast at level 6; Necklace of Missiles: fireballs at level 5. Potions: Healing 2d4+2, Extra Healing 3d8+3, Speed (hasted 6 rounds), Invisibility. Dragonlance and Mace of Disruption: double damage against dragons / undead; sword +4 vs reptiles: +3 more against draconians and dragons. Gauntlets of ogre power: strength 18/00; girdle of giant strength: +3 to hit, +7 damage. | `remake/kroc/magic_items.py` |
| Raise Dead | Elves cannot be raised; survival chance by constitution (40% at 3 to 100% at 18, manual p.55); survivors lose a point of constitution, the others are gone for good | `remake/kroc/camp_magic.py` |
| The gods' special spells | One special slot, two from cleric level 5 (the manual gives no count) | `GOD_SPELLS`, `slots` in `magic.py` |
| Knights' tithe | Not applied: with one shared purse it would empty the whole party's money | — |
| New characters | Starting experience by the manual (second level; clerics and knights first); a starting kit by class (knights: plate, shield, long sword, as the manual says; kender: a hoopak); a starting grimoire by robe; 3d6 x 10 steel (x 2 for knights) | `remake/kroc/creation.py` |
| Monsters' special abilities | From the affect codes in `MONnSPC.DAX`, with AD&D/Dragonlance effects: breath = the dragon's hit points (save for half), three a day; dragon fear on those of fewer hit dice; bozak bones 1d6 and kapak acid 1d6 to those adjacent; paralysis 2-6 rounds; venom 2d6 (snake) or 1d6 (centipede) and poisoned; stench -2 to hit | `remake/kroc/specials.py` |
| Turning undead | d20 against 7 + 3 x (hit dice - cleric level), 2d6 hit dice of undead within 6 squares; 4 levels above destroys | `specials.turn_undead` |
| A mage's new spell | Chosen from the spells open to the mage's order (manual p.54) | `training.WHITE`, `training.RED` |
| Moons | Solinari 36 days, Lunitari 28, Nuitari 8, all full on day 1. Waxing: +1 spell. High sanction: +2 spells, +1 to saves, +1 level (level 6+, INT 15+). Low sanction: -1 save, -1 level. | `magic.MOONS`, `magic.PHASE_EFFECT` |
| Spell effects | AD&D spell descriptions: ranges, areas, durations, saves | `TABLE` in `remake/kroc/spells.py` |
| Sleep, Hold and coup de grace | Sleep affects 4 hit dice or fewer; a sleeping or held victim struck in melee dies | `spells.py`, `Battle.swing` in `combat.py` |
| Morale | Rolled the first time half a monster's side is down, and the first time it falls below a third of its HP. Morale is 40 + 6 per hit die (max 95). Undead and golems never run; a lone monster never runs; a cornered one fights on. Monsters that run give no experience. | `encounter.morale`, `Battle.check_morale` |
| Saving throws (party) | AD&D tables by class and level; paladins +2 | `Character.save_spell` in `world.py` |
| Coin values | 1 steel = 2 platinum = 5 bronze = 10 copper = 50 silver (manual p.4) | `COIN_VALUE` in `world.py` |
| Selling | Half the item's value | `ShopView.sell` in `remake/kroc/inventory.py` |
| Identifying | 100 steel (the original's price) | `IDENTIFY_PRICE` in `inventory.py` |
| Gems and jewelry | A gem is worth 10-500 steel, jewelry 300-1800 | `ShopView.sell_gems` |
| Temple healing | 5 steel per hit point | `TempleView.PER_HP` |
| Random treasure (`TREASURE` item block 128 + n) | n items drawn from all item records on the disks | `World.treasure` |
| Potions of healing | Healing 2d4+2, Extra Healing 3d8+3 | `ItemsView.use` |

## Bugs fixed

These were found while rebuilding the engine. Each one changes what you see
in play.

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| The scripts could not tell which room or area of a map the party was in (`C04F`, the GEO square flags, always read 0). Area events never fired: the guards at Throtl's gate were skipped and the party walked straight in. | `C04F` returns the party's square flags. The gate encounter and the other room events now happen as written. |
| Readying different weapons or armour changed nothing: AC, THAC0 and damage were the save disk's figures | They are worked out from the readied items. The formula gives the saved party's figures exactly, and changing equipment now counts. |
| Experience started at 0 | Read from the character record (offset 0x11E). |
| `TREASURE` handed out loot before the fight it belongs to | The loot is held until the fight is won, then handed out. |
| Shops and temples opened an empty fight | The scripts open them through `COMBAT` with a flag set (`7F6C` shop, `7EE2` temple); the remake opens the armoury or temple instead. |
| Scripts that asked for a number or a name (the vault's "how many will you deposit?") got 0 | INPUT NUMBER and INPUT STRING open a typed prompt. |
| The character window (`7C00`-`7DFF`) always read 0, so the vault saw no money and no characters | LOAD CHARACTER selects who the window shows; `7CC3` is the steel carried (the shared purse, held by the first character) and `7D00` says whether a character is there. |
| ADD NPC was read with one operand instead of two (the companion and its morale), so the morale byte read as EXIT and the scripts stopped where a companion should join | Two operands; the companions join. |
| DAMAGE, ROB, FIND ITEM, DESTROY ITEMS, CHECKPARTY, SPELL and ADD NPC were only logged: traps did no harm, quest items were never checked | All carried out (see FORMATS.md). |
| A trap that killed the whole party left the game running | The party perishes as after a lost fight. |
| Saved items read a plus of +104 | That byte is leftover memory; the real plus is two bytes later (the SWG records are word-aligned). |
| Area spells were blocked by creatures standing in the way | Only walls block a spell's line of sight. |
| A creature asleep or held could still make free attacks and stop archers shooting | Only creatures able to act count as a threat. |
| The combat log printed "shoots at BOZAK. and misses" | Fixed wording. |
| Spell slots followed the AD&D tables, so Red Robes and neutral clerics had the wrong number of spells | Krynn's own tables from the manual. |
| Any mage could scribe any scroll | A Red Robe can only use Red Robe scrolls and a White Robe White ones (manual p.17). |

How the data formats were decoded, including these offsets, is in
[FORMATS.md](FORMATS.md).

## Not yet rebuilt

* a few monster affect codes are not used yet: 0x04, 0x0D, 0x38 (auraks,
  Myrtani), 0x47-0x4E (Sir Lebaum), 0x67 (spectral minion), 0x5B, 0x5C
  (kender), 0x5F (elves)
